newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Good foreign buying buoyed South Africa long bonds on Thursday, leading the market more than 15 basis points stronger on the day, but traders were not convinced that the spurt firmer could be sustained.
At 1415 GMT government's R150 loan was yielding 14.71 percent from 14.845 percent late on Wednesday and a morning high of 14.87 percent.
"Offshore players moved in at lunch-time and almost rigged the market, pushing yields lower in thin volumes," said a senior debt trader.
The steady rand and firmer U.S. Treasurise had also helped the market.
Local institutions had shown some interest at the higher levels, buying longer-dated stock including R153's and R157's.
"The move today was fairly positive but I'm not convinced (that it's a real break)," the dealer added.
The market was still too long on stock before the next step in foreign exchange control easing on July 1 and investors were bound to continue lightening positions.

In the medium-term the outlook was positive but in the short-term there was more potential for the upside until there was more certainty on the amounts of cash that would flow out when exchange controls on individuals were eased.
Some debt traders expected a test of the higher 14.91 to 15 percent levels until month-end.
On Friday, the market was seen retracing back to 14.80 percent.
"Nobody is negative and fundamentally the market is still looking good but sentiment is cautious ahead of forex controls," said a second trader.

Comments by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals reported on Thursday that an early interest rate cut appeared unlikely in the light of excessive money supply growth elicited little reaction from the local debt market.
"It's in line with what he's been saying all along and all it does is inject more caution ahead of the forex easing," one dealer said.
The pricing and maturity of South Africa's second Yankee bond issue late on Wednesday was seen positive, underlining improving foreign investor confidence, dealers said.
Lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co Inc announced that South Africa had raised $500 million over 20 years at a 183 basis point spread above similar dated U.S. Treasuries.
Foreigners were net buyers of 146.29 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 105.00 million rands worth on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative bond market volumes were at 6.4 billion rand on Wednesday from 6.2 billion rand on Tuesday.
On the forex market, the rand managed to regain its composure after an initial run higher as London players sought dollars.
At 1440 GMT the currency was at 4.5110/5140 against the U.S. dollar from 4.5125/5155 late on Wednesday.
It bounced off its weakest morning level of a 4.5175 bid after running into dollar supply by the Reserve Bank and exporters.
German and London banks then sold dollars in the afternoon and this, coupled with local profit-taking, lead the unit to the day's best bid of 4.5070.
"The market got itself long, waiting for a break of 4.52 over the last few days which failed to materialise and now we are seeing local and offshore off-loading of dollars," said one forex trader.
He expected a 4.5070 to 4.5150 range on Friday and players to re-assess positions afresh at the start of next week.
Another senior dealer had a similar view, saying the rand market appered to be getting long dollars and the move higher was gradually losing momentum.

Against the crosses, the rand was last at 25.2503/2893 against the yen from 25.0288/0676 on Wednesday, at 0.3823/3827 marks from 0.3821/3826 marks and at 7.4219/4332 against sterling from 7.3968/4062 previously.
On the money market, short-term rates were unchanged with three-month NCDs quoted at 16.05 percent offered and the 90-day BA rate also steady at between 15.45 to 15.60 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage eased slightly to 7.314 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.324 billion rand on Tuesday, the Reserve Bank said.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482-1003
